<repaired_code>
import java.util.*;
import java.io.*;

public class _1599_C {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        String[] parts = br.readLine().split(" ");
        int n = Integer.parseInt(parts[0]);
        double target = Double.parseDouble(parts[1]);
        
        // If n < 3, there's only one possible set of maps (all maps)
        if (n < 3) {
            System.out.println(n);
            return;
        }
        
        int total = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6; // C(n,3)
        int result = n;
        
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            double prob = 0.0;
            
            // Case 1: Exactly 1 studied map in the 3 selected
            // We need the opponent to discard the other 2 maps, leaving our studied map
            // Probability: C(i,1) * C(n-i,2) / C(n,3) * (1/2) [since opponent picks randomly among 2 unstudied]
            if (n - i >= 2) {
                long ways = (long) i * (n - i) * (n - i - 1) / 2;
                prob += (double) ways / total * 0.5;
            }
            
            // Case 2: Exactly 2 studied maps in the 3 selected
            // We need at least one of us to discard the unstudied map
            // If both opponents discard randomly, probability that unstudied map is discarded by at least one
            // Actually: if we have 2 studied and 1 unstudied, we both want to discard the unstudied one
            // Each player picks randomly among 3, so probability unstudied is discarded by at least one
            // = 1 - P(both pick studied) = 1 - (2/3)*(2/3) = 1 - 4/9 = 5/9? 
            // But problem says: "each player must pick one of those three maps to be discarded"
            // Then system randomly selects one of maps not picked by any player
            // If 2 studied (S1,S2) and 1 unstudied (U):
            // - If both players discard U, then S1 and S2 remain, system picks randomly -> prob 1/2 to get studied
            // - If one discards U and one discards S1, then remaining are S1,S2 (S1 was picked by one but not both? Wait)
            // Actually: "randomly selects one of the maps that were not picked by any of the players"
            // So if players discard different maps, the remaining map is the one neither discarded
            // Let's reconsider:
            // With 2 studied (S1,S2) and 1 unstudied (U):
            // Each player picks one to discard. Possible discard pairs:
            // (U,U): remaining {S1,S2}, system picks randomly -> prob 1 to get studied (since both remaining are studied)
            // (U,S1): remaining {S2}, prob 1 to get studied
            // (U,S2): remaining {S1}, prob 1 to get studied
            // (S1,U): remaining {S2}, prob 1 to get studied
            // (S2,U): remaining {S1}, prob 1 to get studied
            // (S1,S1): remaining {S2,U}, system picks randomly -> prob 1/2 to get studied
            // (S1,S2): remaining {U}, prob 0 to get studied
            // (S2,S1): remaining {U}, prob 0 to get studied
            // (S2,S2): remaining {S1,U}, system picks randomly -> prob 1/2 to get studied
            // 
            // Actually, let's be more careful. Each player independently picks one of the 3 to discard.
            // There are 3*3 = 9 equally likely outcomes.
            // 
            // For case with 2 studied (S1,S2) and 1 unstudied (U):
            // - Both discard U: remaining {S1,S2}, system picks randomly -> prob 1 (both are studied)
            // - Player1 discards U, Player2 discards S1: remaining {S2} -> prob 1
            // - Player1 discards U, Player2 discards S2: remaining {S1} -> prob 1
            // - Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards U: remaining {S2} -> prob 1
            // - Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards U: remaining {S1} -> prob 1
            // - Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S1: remaining {S2,U}, system picks randomly -> prob 1/2
            // - Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S2: remaining {U} -> prob 0
            // - Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards S1: remaining {U} -> prob 0
            // - Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards S2: remaining {S1,U}, system picks randomly -> prob 1/2
            // 
            // Total probability = (2 + 2 + 2 + 0.5 + 0.5) / 9 = 7/9? Wait let me recount:
            // Cases with prob 1: (U,U), (U,S1), (U,S2), (S1,U), (S2,U) = 5 cases
            // Cases with prob 1/2: (S1,S1), (S2,S2) = 2 cases
            // Cases with prob 0: (S1,S2), (S2,S1) = 2 cases
            // Total = (5*1 + 2*0.5 + 2*0) / 9 = (5 + 1) / 9 = 6/9 = 2/3
            // 
            // Actually wait, I think I miscounted. Let me list all 9:
            // 1. P1=U, P2=U: remaining {S1,S2}, prob=1
            // 2. P1=U, P2=S1: remaining {S2}, prob=1
            // 3. P1=U, P2=S2: remaining {S1}, prob=1
            // 4. P1=S1, P2=U: remaining {S2}, prob=1
            // 5. P1=S1, P2=S1: remaining {S2,U}, prob=1/2
            // 6. P1=S1, P2=S2: remaining {U}, prob=0
            // 7. P1=S2, P2=U: remaining {S1}, prob=1
            // 8. P1=S2, P2=S1: remaining {U}, prob=0
            // 9. P1=S2, P2=S2: remaining {S1,U}, prob=1/2
            // 
            // So prob = (1+1+1+1+0.5+0+1+0+0.5)/9 = 6/9 = 2/3
            // 
            // So for exactly 2 studied maps, probability = 2/3
            
            if (i >= 2 && n - i >= 1) {
                long ways = (long) (i * (i - 1) / 2) * (n - i);
                prob += (double) ways / total * (2.0 / 3.0);
            }
            
            // Case 3: All 3 studied maps
            // Then whatever is discarded, the remaining map(s) will all be studied
            // If 3 studied, then remaining map is always studied, prob = 1
            if (i >= 3) {
                long ways = (long) i * (i - 1) * (i - 2) / 6;
                prob += (double) ways / total;
            }
            
            if (prob >= target) {
                result = i;
                break;
            }
        }
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}
